full_judgment:
Hasan Foez Siddique J. This Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.127(Transfer) of 2020 has been filed by the petitioner for withdrawal and transfer of Criminal Appeal No.11784 of 2017 pending before a Division Bench of the High Court Division presided by Mr. Md. Nazrul Islam Talukder and Mr. K.M. Hafizul Alam, J.J. 

 2. Short facts for the disposal of this petition are that the petitioner was convicted by the learned Special Judge, Jessore in Special Case No.02 of 2010 arising out of Jhenidah Police Station Case No.21 dated 14.12.2008 corresponding to G.R. No.740 of 2008 and sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for a period of 3(three) years and to pay fine of tk.20,000/-, in default, to suffer rigorous imprisonment for a further period of 3 (three) years under section 26(2) of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 and he was also sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for a period of 7(seven) years and to pay a fine of tk.50,000/-, in default, to suffer rigorous imprisonment for a period of 6(six) months under section 27(1) of the said Act. He preferred appeal in the High Court Division and obtained bail. 

 3. The said criminal appeal is pending in the aforesaid bench of the High Court Division. At this stage, he has filed this Criminal Miscellaneous Case for transfer of the appeal from the aforesaid bench to another bench of competent jurisdiction. 

 6. It appears from the materials on record that this criminal appeal was preferred in 2017 and a Division Bench of the High Court Division admitting the appeal enlarged the appellant-petitioner on bail for a period of 6(six) months which was subsequently extended time to time. Lastly, a Division Bench presided by Md. Nazrul Islam Talukder, J. extended the order of bail of the petitioner for a period of 3(three) months from date. The Court found that the paper books of the appeal have not been prepared as yet. In such circumstances, the said Bench directed the petitioner to prepare paper book out of Court within 3(three) months with a default order that in case of failure to prepare the requisite number of paper books within the said period, the order of bail shall stand cancelled. 

 7. Considering the facts and circumstances stated above, it is difficult to accept the submission of the learned Counsel of the petitioner that the petitioner would not get proper justice from the Judges of the said Bench since such type of direction to prepare paper books out of Court is not unprecedented and unusual in the process adopted by the High Court Division. A case is to be transferred when there is reasonable apprehension on the part of a party to a case that proper justice will not be done by that Bench. The apprehension of not getting a fair and impartial hearing and disposal of the appeal is required to be reasonable and not imaginary and same must not be based upon conjectures or surmises.
